questions.question: Discuss the contribution of mobile phones to television viewership patterns.

questions.question: Explain cross-promotion with an example.
questions.solution_html:
• Cross-promotion is a marketing strategy where two or more entities promote each other’s
  • products, services, or content to their respective audiences, enhancing visibility and mutual
  • benefit. In television, it involves promoting one program or channel withi n another to boost
  • viewership.
  • Example: A TV network airs a popular reality show and promotes an upcoming drama series
  • during its commercial breaks or as in-show mentions (e.g., a host announcing, “Stay tuned for
  • the premiere of next week!”). This leverages the reality show’s large audience
  • to drive viewership for the new drama, increasing overall channel engagement.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: to drive viewership for the new drama, increasing overall channel engagement.

questions.question: Explain the structure of a TV debate.
questions.solution_html:
• Introduction: Host presents topic, participants, and rules.
  • Opening Statements: Participants state their positions.
  • Main Discussion: Moderated arguments, counterpoints, and questions.
  • Audience Interaction (optional): Questions from viewers.
  • Closing Statements: Participants summarize views.
  • Conclusion: Host recaps and wraps up.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: Conclusion: Host recaps and wraps up.

questions.question: Identify principles of sound recording applied in post-production.
questions.solution_html:
• Noise Reduction: Remove unwanted sounds.
  • Equalization: Balance frequency levels.
  • Compression: Even out volume.
  • Reverb/Effects: Add depth or mood.
  • Mixing: Blend audio tracks.
  • Panning: Distribute sound spatially.
  • Normalization: Standardize volume.
  • Syncing: Align audio with visuals.
  • Restoration: Fix distorted audio.
  • Mastering: Optimize final audio.

questions.question: Evaluate the contributions of Doordarshan in the growth of Indian television.
questions.solution_html:
• Infrastructure Development: Pioneered TV broadcasting from 1959, expanded to
  • national satellite network by 1982, reaching 90% of households.
  • Educational Impact: Launched programs like Krishi Darshan (1967) and SITE (1975
  • 76) for rural education on farming, health, and literacy.
  • Cultural Influence: Iconic shows like Hum Log, Ramayan, and Mahabharat drew
  • millions, fostering shared cultural experiences.
  • News and Unity: Professional news since 1965 built trust, promoted national integration
  • post-1976 AIR separation.
  • Commercial Foundation: Attracted advertisers, enabled private production, and spurred
  • post-1991 TV boom with 800+ channels.
  • Digital Adaptation: Offers DD Free Dish and archives 500,000+ hours, competing with
  • modern platforms like YouTube.

questions.question: Examine the role of the Editorial Board in ensuring ethical practices in news reporting.
questions.solution_html:
• Sets Ethical Standards : Establishes guidelines for accuracy, fairness, and objectivity in
  • reporting.
  • Oversees Content: Reviews stories to ensure compliance with ethical norms and legal
  • regulations.
  • Addresses Bias: Monitors and corrects partiality or sensationalism to maintain credibility.
  • Handles Complaints : Investigates ethical breaches and public grievances, ensuring
  • accountability.
  • Guides Training: Promotes journalist training on ethical practices and editorial integrity.
  • Upholds Public Trust : Ensures transparent, balanced reporting to maintain audience
  • confidence.
